render.prompt:
Image 1 is a real phone photo of a room to edit. Image 2 is a placement guide: the same photo with numbered translucent boxes showing where each product goes; use it only for position and scale and never draw its boxes or numbers. Images 3 to 5 are the reference photos of products 1 to 3, in order.
1. Replace the dark brown three-seat sofa with product 1: Low Back Linen Sofa (sofa), real size 221 x 71.1 x 91.4 cm (width x depth x height). Centered against the window wall where the old dark sofa stands, facing the TV. It belongs inside box 1 of the placement guide. Copy product 1 exactly from its reference photo: Low-profile three-seat sofa in beige linen with wide arms, three loose back cushions, and thin dark tapered legs. Same shape, proportions, color, material, texture, pattern and details, scaled to its real size relative to the room.
2. Add product 2: Cream geometric wool area rug (rug), real size 243.8 x 152.4 x 1.3 cm (width x depth x height). Laid flat on the wood floor centered under the glass coffee table extending beyond it on all sides. It belongs inside box 2 of the placement guide. Copy product 2 exactly from its reference photo: Rectangular cream wool rug with subtle geometric criss-cross texture shown in angled perspective view. Same shape, proportions, color, material, texture, pattern and details, scaled to its real size relative to the room.
3. Add product 3: White Tripod Shelf Floor Lamp (floor lamp), real size 40.6 x 40.6 x 147.3 cm (width x depth x height). Stands on the floor in the back corner between the sofa right arm and the TV stand, shade above sofa height. It belongs inside box 3 of the placement guide. Copy product 3 exactly from its reference photo: White tripod floor lamp with round fabric drum shade, central pole, circular light wood tray table and slender splayed legs. Same shape, proportions, color, material, texture, pattern and details, scaled to its real size relative to the room.
Hard rules: keep the exact same camera position, framing, lens distortion and perspective. Keep the walls, wallpaper, floor, ceiling, ceiling light, windows, blinds or curtains, doors and every object that is not listed exactly as they are. Keep the existing light direction, color temperature and exposure; new products receive the same light and cast soft, physically plausible contact shadows. The result must look like an unedited phone photo of the same room, not a render. Do not add anything else: no extra decor, no text, no numbers, no colored boxes or outlines.
